_contract: Page-edge decision rules (accommodation strategy 'page-edge-rules', NOTATION_ARCHITECTURE §3 item 5): stored as RULES, not baked positions (P6). The splicer (notation/lib/splice.js) consults these; changing a rule re-plans every page on the next render.
_doc_cutPreference: candidates are scored: fewest SEVERED beamable pairs across ALL interrupted sub-beat chunks (stamp-atomic; grids in different parts can be incommensurate, so any chunk still left off its grid is RECORDED in the page's offGrid list, never silent) · then fewest interrupted chunks (by MATERIAL extent, not span) · ties toward the target time
_doc_musicStartBuffer: RUNNING_LOG §404 (2026-09-11, the composer, on a viola note sitting on the alto clef at 35.4 s: 'in the tuba score we had a buffer zone after the clef'): a page CUT can land exactly on a note's onset, and then that note's go line sits at x = gutterPx while everything drawn BEFORE the go line — the notehead unit, its accidental and ledgers, measured at up to 3.44 ss — falls inside the gutter, on top of the clef. The page window therefore opens this many staff spaces EARLY, so the first note's ink starts clear of the gutter. Stated in ss because ss-per-pixel and pixels-per-second both scale with the zoom, so one number holds in the video frame, the ×2 zoom and any export. 0 = the old behaviour.
_doc_edgeReserve: PLAN 2b.7.2/2b.7.3, D59 (2026-09-17): a PRINTED page owns [cut, next cut), so a page window must be WIDER than what it owns — an owned strike inks backwards along its GC arc (pre = 0.36 s at the default preset) and forwards through the rebound (post = 0.24 s). export_print derives leftReserve = max(musicStartBufferSs, GC.pre + this margin) and rightReserve = GC.post + this margin, then plans pages at pageSeconds MINUS both, so every owned strike is whole on its own page and nothing lands in the clef gutter. Stated in staff spaces for the same reason musicStartBufferSs is: one number holds at any zoom. This margin covers what the arc itself does not — the impact dot, the stroke widths, the marks beside the head. Raise it only if tools/check_print_edges.js reports an event that is not whole.
_doc_alwaysShown: the clef pins to the view's left edge and part labels always draw — render behavior, not rules; only tempoLabelContinuation is rule-gated here
_doc_screenPlan: LGMF PLAN 2c.2 (2026-09-25, RUNNING_LOG §340 — the composer: 'the priority here is consistant end/begining of page; so scrolling cursor starts each screen at the same point and ends at the same point on the screen'): 'tile' = Splice.tilePages — every SCREEN page (the app's video and zoom views, export_video) is one fixed span from the IR's start, t0 and tω at the same x on every page, nothing shown twice, the film turning AT tω; musicStartBufferSs does not apply on screen. Absent = planPages, the film's old overlap. PRINT is not affected (export_print plans its own pages).
_doc_printPlan: LGMF PLAN 2c.6 (2026-09-25, NOTATION_STANDARDS §5 — the composer: 'fit in as much as possible on the page before the page turn'): 'objects' = Splice.planObjectPages — the PRINT cut placed by the objects, as late as their rules (edge.<kind>.print) allow: an object that would be split is pushed whole and the cut moves back to its ink start, a pushed GC opening the next page at the top of its descent; the system ends AT the cut; D59's reserves (musicStartBufferSs, edgeReserveMarginSs) do not apply to print. A block of objects longer than a page is cut where it breaks the fewest, each broken object kept whole on the page owning its onset (the page recorded 'forced'). Absent = planPages with D59's reserves.
_doc_durationStubSs: LGMF PLAN 2c.6: a duration line (edge print 'stub') may take the print cut only if its head and this much of its line fit before it; else it goes over whole. PROVISIONAL — his words, §340: 'I have to see it to make a decision precisely'; judged on the proof when the notation is in (§347).
_doc_leadInS: LGMF PLAN 2e.2 (his word 2026-09-27, RUNNING_LOG §409: '4s for presentation score, but let's revisit for rehearsal and performance versions'): THE LEAD-IN — the piece's 0 sits leadInS seconds into the first page. SCREEN: the tiling opens at the IR's start − leadInS (every page still one span; Splice.screenStartOf), the app's clock runs from −leadInS and the ♪ render starts when it crosses 0; the VIDEO frames from −leadInS and its audio is delayed by the same (ffmpeg -itsoffset); PAPER: page 1 is placed by its objects — its window opens where the first unit's ink begins (Splice.planObjectPages firstByObjects), as a pushed GC places the next page. The WAV is untouched. A realization may override it (realizations.<name>.leadInS); absent = 0 = no lead-in, today's page exactly.
_doc_clampGoLine: LGMF PLAN 2c.6 (his '2a', 2026-09-25): a SCREEN unit clamped right of x(t0) with no go-time indicator of its own — 'flag' (the default) = reported by tools/check_screen_edges.js · 'add' = it takes a go line at x(t), its time exact (PLAN 2c.4 (b), one per note). His decision, deferred to the specific notation (RUNNING_LOG §347).

edge._doc: LGMF PLAN 2c (2026-09-25, RUNNING_LOG §340): THE EDGE CLASS OF EVERY DRAWN KIND (render.js item kinds). print (2c.6, NOTATION_STANDARDS §5 — the table and its basis): 'whole' = on the page owning its time, complete, never cut · 'stub' = may take the cut once its head + durationStubSs fit, else over whole · 'never-sever' = no cut inside it · 'continue' = broken at the cut and continued, following its note · 'furniture' = the page's own. screen: 'cut' = drawn on every page it crosses, clipped at [x(t0), x(tω)] like paper, the remainder picked up at the next t0 at the same height (2c.3) · 'clamp' = a point item of the note unit: owned by the page with t0 <= t < tω, and if the unit's ink hangs left of x(t0) it is shifted right by the difference (2c.4) · 'atomic' = a GO-TIME INDICATOR: owned the same way, drawn at x(t) to the pixel, never moved, never clipped · 'furniture' = the page's own (staff, clef), not the music's. boundary 'before' = an item exactly at tω belongs to the page BEFORE (the GC impact: the performer sees it before the eye moves). The PLAN header's standing rule: every item that draws a NEW kind adds its line here; a kind with no entry fails tools/check_screen_edges.js. Read only on a tiled screen page — absent = today's behaviour.

hairpin-timed._note: LGMF PLAN 2g (§466): the vibraphone's TIMED hairpin spans the time of its movement — a spanning graphic like the ring bar it lies under, so it takes the ring bar's classes: cut like paper on screen, a stub at a print cut; the 2f `hairpin` (a fixed-length symbol) keeps clamp · whole

slash._note: §550: the grace note's stroke — a point kind on the grace's stem

slur._note: §555: a slur spans its notes (t0 · t1) — cut like paper on screen; on paper the cut is placed so a slur is never severed (the beam's class; splice.js reads t0 · t1)

gc._note: the ARC is cut like paper; the IMPACT is a go-time indicator at x(t), owned (t0, tω] — at exactly tω on the page before

beam._note: drawn through every tip on a page it crosses, clipped; each tip follows its unit's clamp

bowlead._note: §495 (2i.7): the bow lead — a point item at its head's time, a clamped stamp on screen, whole on paper, like the head it hangs from

headswatch._note: §495: the head swatch — a point item behind its head, the head's classes

edge._doc_animated: LGMF PLAN 2e.2 (RUNNING_LOG §409 … §411, his word 'one system, not a separate one'): THE ANIMATED KINDS (notation/lib/animobj.js, redrawn every frame at the now) as `anim:<kind>`, under the same classes, through the one edge function (notation/lib/edge_rules.js): the cursor 'atomic' (the now itself — never moved) · the meters, the pies, the follower dots 'clamp' — at a page start a device whose proper place is left of x(t0) is PUSHED RIGHT, one push per lane, and slides back as the cursor advances (his 'ok for this one pushed right', §411) · the GC ball 'cut' (it rides its arc, which is cut) · print 'none' for all: paper has no now (§410 (B), the AI's call). A new animated kind adds its line here or tools/check_rules.js fails; tools/check_screen_edges.js probes each page's first and last frame.
